Playable Classes

Reminder: As explained earlier in our rules, each Race features Favored and Averse main classes, dealing various bonuses and penalties respectively. See Favored and Averse Class Bonuses and Penalties under each Playable Race's entry, at Playable Races, pg. 2.

When dealing with Classes, it is also important to note a character's alignment determines which classes they can access Nature or spells from. Classes themed by alignment require the character to already hold that alignment before any of that class's nature or spells can be chosen.

Alignment itself is determined by their background. When a background is selected (whether from a module's curated options or a custom background created with the GM), the GM confirms the character's alignment based on that background's moral and ethical elements immediately.

Once the character's background is confirmed by the player and GM, it locks in and cannot be changed. The player then chooses their race followed by their class, and while most classes remain open regardless of alignment, a few require a specific one.

For example, a character with an alignment of Lawful cannot choose Nature or spells from Doom Knight, an Evil-aligned class, unless their alignment later shifts to Evil through the bad deeds and choices they've made during adventuring, a shift that may happen rapidly or slowly depending on the nature of their practices.

Independent of alignment and a race's Favored or Averse standing, every main class tree also has its own required readied Armaments. This readied Armament Set consists of one donned armor piece and up to three carried weapon types, held for at least 24 hours before a new Armament Set can be readied. A weapon in hand may be swapped for a sheathed one to change which Nature or spells are accessible, at the cost of a turn to do so. Depending on what's donned or in hand, a character is either restricted from using certain Nature or spells outright, or sustains the Penalties described under Armaments, pg. 6.

After choosing their race, a player chooses their main class. At each Character Level, they gain one Ability (Nature/Spell) pick to spend from their active main class tree(s), alignment permitting†, and a second pick at the midpoint toward the next Character Level, each pick filling one open Slot in a tree. Any pick can go toward the same tree as the one before it, advancing it a further Slot, or toward a different tree the character has access to. Within any single Slot, a player still chooses only one Ability out of the 3 available (see Slots and Prerequisites, below). At Slot 4 of a tree, its Path opens, letting a character continue investing in that tree's Path, or begin choosing from another main class tree's Tier instead, again alignment permitting. Staying on one main class's Path from Slot 4 through Slot 20, then continuing into that Path's Branch through Slot 30, maxes out that tree, which can only be done once since the Ability cap is 59 (see Class Tree Development, below, for the full pacing and capstone rules).

†Remember, some classes require a specific alignment, such as the Avenger requiring Lawful alignment.

Every Ability roll made in that class is then modified by the race's Favored or Averse standing toward it (see Favored and Averse Class Bonuses, pg. 2), along with Traits, buffs from magic or advantages, and other enhancements, such as those from Armaments.

Characters can carry any Armaments they want, so long as they can bear the weight. Characters can only ready a restricted loadout, three main and/or offhand weapons, ammunition and armor, at the start of each game day, and must keep that set for at least one day - 24 game hours (see Weapons Carried, pg. 4).

Abilities may be chosen from any tree the character wants, sequentially and progressively or sporadically, but they cannot be used unless the required Armaments are not only readied, but donned and drawn. Each readied loadout can be kept as long as the player chooses for their character, there's no expiration, but it must stay intact for at least 24 game hours, the next game day, before changing to a new Armament Set.

For example, a character can have a 1h holy hammer and shield readied and drawn while wearing chain armor, and use Abilities from the Cleric path (see Avenger) beginning at level 4.

At level 4, they could choose a Nature from the Monk path, but would have to doff the chain and sheath the 1h holy hammer and shield in exchange for any wooden blunt weapons and light or delicate armor before using Monk path Nature. The cloth or delicate armor and wood-only blunt weapon must be readied, even if it's respectively doffed and sheathed. Light and delicate armors are light in weight, so having either readied and carried doesn't require much in terms of strength. Three main weapons may be readied (drawn or sheathed) and switched at will, at the cost of their turn. Smaller weapons listed as ammunition (throwing daggers x3 per boot, one throwing axe per hip, etc., arrows in a quiver, etc.) are separate and don't need to be readied, but the character must be able to bear their weight and have the tools to carry them, for instance, quivers, sheaths, holsters, boot straps, belt straps, and so on.

Characters may switch in and out of Armaments at will, at the cost of the turn, as long as the Armaments are readied. They may carry as many as their strength/encumbrance will allow, including with the assistance of Companions, such as a Pack Mule, NPC Henchmen, and so forth, but this only makes them available, not readied, which can only be done every 24 hours.

Just as with main classes, each path and branch defines its own Armament Prerequisites that must be met to use its Abilities (see Basic Rules pg. 6). In terms of armor, paths are restricted by Grade, with Composite being the heaviest and Delicate the lightest. A path's armor threshold includes every Grade lighter than it: for instance, if Medium Grade is allowed, Light and Delicate are as well.

Weapons are required or restricted based not only on Style (Slashing, Blunt, Piercing, Chop, etc.), and there are other cases where specific weapons are allowed for certain tree branches, even though the weapon profile was earlier restricted for the main class and path Nature or spells. For instance, the Salii branch of the Priest path may use daggers (must be magic) and Medium Grade armor (again must be magic†), even though up to that point of the Avenger tree, neither is permitted.

†Any item (in this case daggers or Medium Grade armor) that has a magical effect.

To perform Abilities from the Avenger's - Cleric Path - characters are required to have readied a 1h blunt weapon and shield, or a 2h blunt weapon. Either satisfies the Path's Weapon Requirements (see Weapon Requirements, Basic Rules pg. 6), adding a choice of flavor and playstyle.

Maximizing their weight capacity (see Strength and Encumbrance), characters may carry various weapons and armor that allow them to utilize different main class, path and branch fighting styles, as long as these Armaments are readied and donned or drawn - in hand(s).

As Character's progress through a classes linear tier, path and branch, Armament options expand.

One Branch example is the Salii, which extends from the Priest Path, breaks away from Light Armor and 2h Blunt restrictions, allowing Medium Grade armor and Daggers (both must be Magic).

Within the Monk path, the Qirateka Branch eventually allows dual 1h Blunt wielding, or a 2h quarterstaff in the main hand with a small bladed weapon, such as a tonfa or sai, in the offhand.

Another example would be the Main Class Fighter that chooses to excel in the brawler path, where they will use their hands (wrapped) as well as environmental objects, such as; dust and dirt, broken glass, mugs, coin rolls, lamps, and so forth as their weapon choices. These characters will also develop tough skin, often wearing very little to protect themselves relying on their tough skin and urban acrobatics (see Olympiad Tree). Brawlers may wear Medium Grade bracers for their protection as well, giving them an element of parry (see Traits, Defense) for protection.

Certain Classes are also restricted to various modifications. For instance, because the Avenger Class alignment requires Lawful, Salii Priests cannot coat their daggers with poisons or carry other applied effects as a rogue or necromancer can. For a Salii the dagger must be magic and hold no properties such as applying poison. These daggers are only used to strike and cast, applying poisons to them would result in punishment by the Avenger's higher power.

Touching on some of what we've discussed above; Characters can have drawn any weapons, in hand(s), they choose, but they won't be able to perform certain Abilities if the weapons they're holding are not the requirements of that main class tree's Tier, Path and/or Branch.

This means a character that has chosen Nature for a level 4 Monk can obtain a sword, and have it drawn, but they wouldn't be able to perform any of the Nature since they require bare hands or various wood-only blunt weapons. They could use Actions during their turn to swap to a viable weapon, in this case either drop the sword (half an Action) or switch to a blunt/wood weapon (a full Action) if, in the latter case, they have one (of three possible - see readied weapons, pg. 4) readied and on their person.

Or if they have chosen Abilities from another class tree that allows the sword, e.g., Nature from a Warrior Tree, they could just perform those Nature. This system allows characters to hybrid through several classes at one time, sometimes without even changing 1 of 3 readied Armament sets.

However, there are other restrictions that don't allow the use of certain armaments, such as agility Prerequisites for certain ranged Abilities, strength or charisma to wear certain armor, rank restrictions and path restrictions to weapon types; e.g., † Monks can't use edged weapons or blunt weapons made from anything other than wood, † Clerics can't use edged weapons, Warlocks cannot use holy weapons, while Paladins can't use unholy weapons; however Paladins are not restricted to any weapon type, unless they don't meet other requirements, such as the agility Prerequisite to use an offhand dagger.

† Overseers and Avengers cannot use unholy weapons. They must begin to fall, taking penalties and challenges from their respective higher powers to Abilities of said tree(s).

† Fallen and Risen classes, although covered here are pg. 3 covered much more detailed in the GM Codex.

Each main class tree, and its Tier (levels 1-3), follows the same structure through its Path (4-20) into Branch picks (21-30), for a total of 30 (its cap) across the Tier and its respective Path and Branch, growing exponentially in power until the end. With that in mind, the Nature or spell power gap between pick 29 to 30 is the most significant in power of each tree. This gives players tough decisions between choosing raw power, moderate power and some diversity, or raw diversity with less power between their Nature and spells but gives them a wide array of choices per turn.

These Ability variations are derived from different main class tier, path and branch structures. In order for a main class to reach the 30 cap max Abilities, the character would have to choose linearly from Tier, through Path and Branch, staying on the same half of the Split, Nature or Spell, the entire way. The Slot letter itself, A, B, or C, does not need to stay the same and can change freely level to level, only the Nature/Spell half matters for the cap. For instance, an Avenger - Cleric - Warpriest reaches all 30 of the Cleric's Spell by staying on the Spell half at every level from Tier through Branch, picking Slot A at some levels, Slot B or C at others, whichever fits, while never once choosing a Nature instead. This would be the ONLY route to a level 30 cap for that tree, since the Ability cap is 59. Breaking this linear pattern by crossing into the Nature half at any point makes it impossible to reach 30, since each half must independently reach its own count of 30, and splitting Picks between the two means neither one can.

It's important to note that every Main Class runs a Split Tier, Split Path, and Split Branch, such as; Avenger - Cleric, Avenger - Monk, and Strategist - Shadow Stalker, each offering a Split Nature Drawn or Split Spell Drawn half at every level of progression, from Tier through Branch. This holds true without exception across all 16 Main Classes.

The 59 Ability cap (see pg. 3) ensures a character can only fully max one class tree. At most, one tree, from its Tier through Branch, can reach 30, and a second caps at 29 (total of 59). In the case of a Split class, its two halves share that same 30-cap rather than each reaching 30 separately, as long as they stay within the Split type, Nature or Spell. For example, for Classes with Split Paths and Branches, that offer both Nature and Spell (see Cleric), you can reach the 30th Ability choosing either Slot, A, B or C, but must stay within the Nature or Spell split. You can choose between Nature and Spell within the Split, but you'll never reach the 30th respective Ability, because the math doesn't allow it, each half needs its own full 30, and splitting Picks between them keeps both short.

Paths and Branches are freely chosen at Slot 4 and Slot 21 respectively, no earlier Slot choice restricts which one. Separately, certain Slots carry a Prerequisite: every 4th Level starting at Level 3 (3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 27), one Slot, cycling A, B, C, is a Prerequisite for that same Slot and Split at the very next Level. See Slots and Prerequisites, below, for the full rule.

With a limit of 3 readied weapons carried Per Day (see above), a character cannot perform Abilities from every class tree in a single session. They could manage to go through a lot of them, within a day using three distinct weapon types on their person, swapping out at will, however. This makes wide-spread Ability investment genuinely viable for Characters allowing them to continue to choose Abilities throughout various class trees, maximizing only one. Characters without weapon types that adhere to their Abilities, can still use standard or makeshift Combat attacks (see Combat pg. 5). Characters can still hone their skills on crafts and hobbies, utilizing their endurance for the remaining time of the day, during their downtime waiting for the 24 hour readied weapon cool down.

Revisiting Page 2 Content Alignment and Class Compatibility

A character's alignment is determined by their backstory during creation and remains their foundational choice unless altered by decisions characters make during their adventures. Each module provides curated backgrounds with built-in moral and ethical elements related to Lawful, Evil, or Neutral.

Once a background is determined, the GM confirms the character's starting alignment based on that background's elements, alerting the player before confirming. Players can also create custom backgrounds built between themselves and the GM, who sets the alignment.

Alignment determines which classes a character can access. Two classes require Lawful alignment; Avenger and Overseer. Four classes require Evil alignment; Doom Knight, Warlock, Witch, and Tyrant. The remaining ten; Barbarian, Bard, Druid, Fighter, Magic User, Marksman, Shaman, Sorcerer, Strategist, and Warrior, accept all alignments. Once an alignment has been assigned, players select their class(es), Nature or spells from those available to that alignment.

A Lawful character can combine Lawful classes with any neutral class, but cannot hold Evil-tree Abilities. An Evil character can combine Evil classes with any neutral class, but cannot hold Lawful-tree Abilities. A Neutral character can combine Neutral classes together, but cannot select either Lawful-only or Evil-only classes.

Since Alignment shifts over time through a character's choices and actions during play, a character's current alignment position is tracked on the Alignment bar of their Character Sheet's Progression Tracker.

If a character's actions drift significantly from a character's alignment, it may trigger Fallen or Risen mechanics exclusive to that lawful or evil class tree. Falling or Rising characters whose alignment drifts all the way to Neutral can no longer perform or earn new Abilities from the class tree that is either lawful or evil AND they'll begin to take penalties and tests from their respective higher powers.

See Fallen and Risen below, and Titles under Prestige, for how a shifting alignment reshapes a character's class standing.

Class Tree Development

Abilities carry no point cost. A character gains one Ability pick at each Character Level, and a second at the midpoint toward the next Character Level, XP-wise, all the way from Character Level 1 through 30. The one restriction sits on the 30th Ability in any class tree, its capstone: it can only be claimed on a full Character Level, never at a midpoint, no matter how many picks a character has already banked toward that tree. Once chosen, an Ability is available whenever its required armament is equipped (for martial Nature) or drawn (for casting Abilities).

Starter Set

The Starter Set covers levels 1-5 for six curated classes and five curated races, fully supported with Nature Cards, Spell Cards, and starting equipment. Additional classes, paths, and races open up in the full ruleset beyond level 5. See Starter Set Overview, Basic Rules pg. 2, for the full description and the Starter Set Playable Races list.

Starter Set Playable Classes: Avenger (Lawful), Barbarian (All), Marksman (All), Sorcerer (All), Strategist (All), Witch (Evil). Each is shown at full opacity below, with its Tier (1-3) and Path (4-5) Nature and/or Spell briefly described, see each respective Nature Card or Spell Card for full details. Everything from Path level 6 onward, and every Branch (21-30), is real structure that exists in the full tree but is dimmed since it's out of reach until later releases unlock it. Every other class below is shown at reduced opacity and is not yet available in the Starter Set.

The 59 Ability Cap, Four Build Examples

A tree's 30th Ability, its capstone, can only be claimed on a full Character Level, never at a midpoint (see Class Tree Development, above). A tree pushed hard from Character Level 1 reaches its 29th pick, one short of its capstone, by Character Level 15. From there, a player can choose to grab that capstone right away on any later Character Level, or hold off and build a second tree instead, spending both later Character Levels and midpoints on it, and only decide which tree gets its true 30th when a Character Level finally comes due. 30 + 29 = 59.

Example 1:

Theron, Warrior / Barbarian Nature picks per level of progression.

30 Nature Warrior Main Class, and 29 Nature Barbarian Main Class for a total of maximum, 59 Nature.

Both neutral trees, no alignment conflict. Theron puts every pick into Warrior from the start:

  • Character Level 1: Warrior's 1st Nature (Tier)
  • Halfway to Level 2 (150† XP, the midpoint between Lvl 1 and Lvl 2): Warrior's 2nd Nature (Tier)
  • Character Level 2: Warrior's 3rd Nature (Tier) - Warrior's Tier is complete
  • Halfway to Level 3: Warrior's 4th Nature (Path begins)

†see pg. 2 for the XP table, covered in full detail in the GM Codex.

He continues this same pattern, one pick at every Character Level and one at every midpoint, sending every pick into Warrior. By Character Level 15, he chooses Warrior's 29th Nature, from the Duelist branch, one short of the capstone, 30. The 30th Ability requires a full Character Level, never a midpoint, and only one can be claimed there.

Theron will need to wait 15 more levels before choosing that 30th Nature.

Capped at 29 in Warrior, through the Blade Master path and into the Duelist branch, Theron reaches Character Level 16 and begins investing in the main class Barbarian, following the same pattern: Tier, Path, then Branch. By Character Level 29, he reaches Barbarian's 28th Nature, and at the midpoint to Level 30 he can choose Barbarian's 29th Nature, from the Ghost branch.

At Level 30, Theron must now choose between the Duelist branch's (Warrior) 30th Nature or the Ghost branch's (Barbarian) 30th Nature. Theron chooses his 30th Nature to cap the Warrior branch, Duelist.

Example 2:

Lyra, Sorcerer / Marksman / Bard Ability picks per level of progression.

20 Spell Sorcerer Main Class, 20 Nature Marksman Main Class, and 19 Spell Bard Main Class for a total of maximum, 59 Abilities.

All three neutral trees, no alignment conflict. Lyra never sends two picks in a row to the same tree, she rotates:

  • Character Level 1: Sorcerer's 1st Spell (Tier)
  • Halfway to Level 2: Marksman's 1st Nature (Tier)
  • Character Level 2: Bard's 1st Spell (Tier)
  • Halfway to Level 3: Sorcerer's 2nd Spell (Tier)

She continues rotating this way for the rest of her career, following her adventures rather than a fixed order. By Character Level 30, her picks land as 20 Spell in Sorcerer (through the Wizard path), 20 Nature in Marksman (through the Bowman path), and 19 Spell in Bard (through the Strumalong path).

None of her three trees ever reach a capstone. A tree's 30th Ability requires being that tree's sole focus, and Lyra never sticks with one long enough to get there.

Example 3:

Varek, 14 trees Ability picks per level of progression.

3 to 5 Abilities in each of 14 Main Classes for a total of maximum, 59 Abilities.

Lawful and Evil trees can never be combined, so the widest possible spread for an Evil-Neutral character draws from 14 trees: Barbarian, Bard, Doom Knight, Druid, Fighter, Magic User, Marksman, Shaman, Sorcerer, Strategist, Tyrant, Warlock, Warrior, and Witch. Varek spreads wide from the start:

  • Character Level 1: Barbarian's 1st Nature (Tier)
  • Halfway to Level 2: Bard's 1st Spell (Tier)
  • Character Level 2: Doom Knight's 1st Ability (Tier)
  • Halfway to Level 3: Druid's 1st Ability (Tier)

He continues cycling through all 14 trees this same way. Each tree picks up 3 Abilities (42 total), then each picks up its 4th, the first step into that tree's Path (14 more, 56 total). Three trees, Barbarian, Doom Knight, and Warlock, go one step further, reaching a 5th Ability each, the last 3 needed to hit 59, the cap.

No tree comes close to its capstone, and no branch is ever reached.

Example 4:

Kestrin, Strategist / Bard / Marksman / Sorcerer / Druid Ability picks per level of progression.

29 Abilities scattered across Bard, Marksman, Sorcerer, and Druid Main Classes, and 30 Abilities Strategist Main Class for a total of maximum, 59 Abilities.

All neutral trees, no alignment conflict. Through Character Level 15, Kestrin's first 29 picks go wherever the story calls for them:

  • Character Level 1: Bard's 1st Spell (Tier)
  • Halfway to Level 2: Marksman's 1st Nature (Tier)
  • Character Level 2: Sorcerer's 1st Spell (Tier)
  • Halfway to Level 3: Druid's 1st Ability (Tier)

She continues cycling this way through her first 29 picks: Bard 8, Marksman 8, Sorcerer 7, Druid 6, none of the four past their Tier and early Path.

Her 30th pick, arriving at the midpoint of Character Level 15, goes toward something new instead, the first Ability of Strategist. From there every remaining pick goes into Strategist alone, reaching 28 by Character Level 29, and 29 at the midpoint toward Level 30. Character Level 30 then delivers Strategist's 30th Ability, its capstone, her 59th pick overall, the cap.

Slots and Prerequisites, at each level of progression, Characters are granted a choice between ONE Nature or spell, or both (since there are two choices per level), of a Tier, Path, or Branch between three slots; A, B or C.

Slot A is a Protector choice (Martial or Magic protection), Slot B is a Damage Dealer choice (Attack), and Slot C is a Heals/Utility choice (single-target heals, group heals, cleanse, survival, buffs and similar support effects), not limited to those examples.

Caster Nature Drawn and Reagents: this is the mirror of Magic Weapons, Nature Drawn, and Spell Drawn (see Basic Rules Appendix): a Martial-tree class (Barbarian, Warrior, Ranger, Rogue, and similar) needs an Enchanted, Magic-Type version of its normal weapon to cast that tree's Spell Drawn abilities, even though those abilities still read as maneuver-flavored, a war cry, a spirit-rite, a chant, they're spell-like, not full spells, carrying spell mechanics despite the physical flavor. The same logic runs the other way for a Caster-tree class (Avenger, Cleric-style Paths, Druid, Sorcerer, Witch, and similar): any Nature Drawn ability of theirs, not limited to heals, also covers wards, cleanses, buffs, marks, and similar support or utility effects, is still struck or channeled through the class's required weapon or implement like any other Nature Drawn ability. It is not a full Spell Drawn ability and costs no Mana, but it's spell-like too, not full nature, it isn't free of a cost either. It requires a reagent as stated on that Ability's Card, and/or direct contact, hand or a class-specific implement (e.g. a holy symbol, totem, or focus) held against the target, whichever the Card specifies. This applies to every Caster-tree class's spell-like abilities alike, not just Heals/Utility, and not just one class.

A character gets one pick at each Character Level, and a second at the midpoint toward the next Character Level (see Class Tree Development, above, for the full pacing and capstone rules). The midpoint is reached when a character's cumulative XP hits the midpoint between their current Ch. Lvl's cumulative XP threshold and the next Ch. Lvl's threshold (see Character Level XP Progression, GM Codex Ch. II); for example, Ch. Lvl 15 sits at 161,300 cumulative XP and Ch. Lvl 16 at 194,100, so the midpoint toward Ch. Lvl 16 falls at 177,700 XP. Each pick fills a different Slot choice, whether the second choice is a linear advancement from the first or from a different main class's path or branch altogether. Once a pick is made, learned from a Class Trainer at a price, it locks in permanently, and there is no reverting.

Tier Abilities (Levels 1-3) are a Main Class's core Abilities, before any Path or Branch, its Sub-Classes, exist yet. At Slot 4, a Path opens, freely chosen among that Main Class's Paths, no earlier Slot choice restricts which one. At Slot 21, a Branch opens the same way, freely chosen among that Path's Branches.

Separately, certain Slot choices carry a Prerequisite. Every 4th Level starting at Level 3 (Levels 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, and 27), one Slot, cycling A, B, C, A, B, C, A, is a Prerequisite for that SAME Slot and SAME Split half (Nature or Spell) at the very next Level. Choosing it doesn't force a character to choose that Slot again next Level, they remain free to pick any Slot or Split they wish, it only unlocks the option to pick that same Slot and Split again. Not choosing it locks that one specific Ability out permanently, once an Ability can no longer be chosen, it's gone for that character for good, though every other Slot and Split at that Level remains freely available regardless.

For example: at Level 3, Slot A is the Prerequisite Slot. If Slot A Spell is chosen at Level 3, the character may then choose Slot A Spell at Level 4, though they're not required to, any other Slot or Split remains just as available. If Slot B Spell was chosen at Level 3 instead, Slot A Spell at Level 4 is locked out permanently, while Slot A Nature, Slot B, and Slot C all remain open regardless.

The next Prerequisite Slot lands at Level 7 (Slot B), then Level 11 (Slot C), then Level 15 (Slot A again), Level 19 (Slot B), Level 23 (Slot C), and Level 27 (Slot A), repeating the same cycle every 4 Levels for the rest of the tree, each one gating that same Slot and Split at the Level directly after it.

For example: a Cleric who picks Slot B (purple) at Level 20 unlocks the Oracle Branch at Level 21; from there, Levels 21 through 30 must be taken one Level at a time, in order, with no skipping.

The Split, Nature or Spell, never matters for either Prerequisite, a Nature or a Spell chosen at Level 3 or Level 20 works equally well to unlock the Path or Branch that Slot leads to. This replaces any earlier chain-style Prerequisites between individual Slot picks; the Level 3 and Level 20 picks are now the only two points in a tree that gate what comes next.

Paths and Branches are Sub-Classes of their Main Class: each Path is a Sub-Class chosen at Level 4, and each Branch is a further Sub-Class chosen at Level 21, continuing that same Path's progression rather than branching into a wholly separate tree.

[Image Placeholder], a screenshot of one Path showing a Level 3 Slot A Prerequisite choice, color-coded, unlocking that same Slot A at Level 4.

Note to writer: Avenger's Cleric Path (see below) has the Slot A/B/C (Protector/Damage Dealer/Heals-Utility, plus Martial/Magic type, damage type, and delivery/target detail) fully applied. Use it as the template for every other class's Tier and Path content that hasn't been converted yet.

Abilities increase in power in sequential order of advancement, with the 30th Ability bearing exponential power over the 29th. As we have learned, Characters are not restricted to only one main class tree's Tier, Path or Branch; which allows multiple trees to create versatile or specialized characters, provided they meet armament and alignment Prerequisites associated with each tree. To learn new Abilities, characters must visit a Class Trainer, usually found in towns or metropolises across Essentia, and must pay a fee (prices vary per area); however, characters may run into NPC Class Trainers in isolated parts of the world, deep underground, deep in the woods, or in a vast desert as well, depending on the setting. This doesn't mean the Trainer will train the character, oftentimes Trainers will require Characters to establish stance with their factions before talking to them, let alone training them, but this usually isn't an issue in towns or large cities.

Class Trainers must be at least the Level of the Character to teach Abilities. Class Trainers only need to be of the Main Class to teach any Tier, Path or Branch within that Main Class, so as long as the Trainer is of the character's Level, they are qualified to teach the character Abilities.

Learning Abilities at the midpoint of the next Level still only requires the Trainer to be of that Level of the character. For instance, if a character is Level 11 and wants to learn his or her 12th Ability at the midpoint to Level 12 (see rules), the Trainer still only needs to be Level 11 and must be a teacher of that main class's tree.

If a character levels up, or reaches a midpoint that grants Ability development, far from a town, for instance deep within a dungeon or remote location, they can potentially use their Wayfarer†, if available, or coordinate with other group members, such as mages (NPC or party), to port into the nearest town or city that would have a Trainer.

†See Animated Wayfarer, Basic Rules pg. 5, for the Faction Sense ability and what a Wayfarer can and can't tell its owner about a town's faction stance. Class faction alone is USUALLY enough stance for a character to learn Abilities, but if not, establishing enough stance within any faction within reason by completing a few quests usually earns the Trainer's trust.

Below are the playable main class trees, their paths and path branches (Abilities for each class under heavy development). Bonuses and Penalties are restrictions and bonuses to equipment. How equipment affects the character beyond the class modifications, such as; "lose a movement then if wearing plate" or "bonus to charisma if wearing plate" is entirely up to how the character plays their role(s), particularly since players can choose as many class trees as they want, as long as they don't exceed the Ability cap.

Main Class Ability Summaries: Tiers, Paths and Branches

For full version see each Ability's Card, per module

Before delving into each playable class's stat card, it's important to point out that playable classes are more than just a consolidation of stats. Playable Classes shape Characters at the table, not just in fighting style but culturally and retrospectively (see backstory) as well.

The Ogre warrior who trusts dual clubs and fur armor over a battle axe and plate, the human sorcerer who chooses a tribal war dress and staff over his well-off relative's robe and crystal-set staff, or the halfling strategist who wins a fight before it ever starts, while his elven comrade in arms chooses the Spellblade role within Strategist.

There are sixteen main classes available: Avenger, Barbarian, Bard, Doom Knight, Druid, Fighter, Magic User, Marksman, Overseer, Shaman, Sorcerer, Strategist, Tyrant, Warlock, Warrior, and Witch. Each runs its own unique Tier, Path, and Branch structure, with some leaning entirely on Nature, some entirely on Spell, and some, such as the Avenger, offering Split choices between both.

Starting with Avenger, the classes below are listed in alphabetical order, with six shown at full opacity, Playable in SORC's Starter Set; while the remaining ten are shown at reduced opacity, their lore still readable, but their full Tier/Path/Branch content still under development for a future release.

‡ IMPORTANT
Below are summarized versions of every Ability. Each Ability comes in the form of SORC Cards released in Modules that reflect the level of the Card. For instance, a Level 4-8 module has every level 4-8 Ability available for every playable class in SORC. As expansions and different versions are released, the content of the Modules will adhere to the new rules and content.

Avenger (Playable in Starter Set)

Alignment Restrictions: Lawful

Faith-driven warriors bound to a higher power, at first restricted to blunt weapons and a light armor default threshold. As with all Paths and Branches, later Avengers unlock some 1h bladed weapons and Medium or Half Medium Armor.

Avengers practice righteous judgment showcasing an array of divine protection, healing, martial combative skills, hand to hand combat and mythical chants guided through their chosen deity or spiritual force. Where others seek to end a fight quickly, an Avenger is built to outlast it, wearing the wicked down through unshakable faith and sheer endurance until judgment finally comes due.

‡ Abilities from their respective trees are summarized below. Ability Cards are released with Module and their expansions, supporting various Character Levels, and list the DIFS for any check an Ability requires. Refer pg. 6 for more on Ability Cards.

Note: Main Class baseline stats, Armament requirements and thresholds, and other Class features change depending on the Classes Tier, Path or Branch as noted in each respective Sub-Class.

Favored Races:
Dwarf (Common)† +5, Human† +5, Firbolg +5, Hawkbear +5

†Dwarf and Human Playable with Starter Set.

Averse Races: Bast -5, Bugbear -5, Troll (Bridge) -5, Troll (Mountain) -5, Drāco Blood -5, Drow -5, Dwarf (Glimmerstone) -5, Gnoll -5, Orcus -5, Goblorc -5, Pinkling -5, Ratkin -5, Emberscale -5, Imperials -5

Refer to Races for details on favored and averse paths and branches.

Passive Abilities:
These passive Abilities belong to the Main Class alone, granted once and active regardless of Tier, Path, or Branch; they are not re-granted, replaced, or duplicated at any Path or Branch.

Avenger Blessing, lasts 6 hours (must be recast every 6 hours to stay active). No mana cost for Main Class Abilities.

Zealous Reckoning, Once Per Day the Avenger calls down judgment, dealing holy damage equal to twice their Piety Score to one target and healing themselves for half that amount.

Extra 1d6 + lvl radiant damage on Critical Hits.
Once per encounter, Avengers can Flourish their blunt weapon to grant an ally a free Defense roll.

Avengers get +5 feet their base movement speed, once per encounter.

Avengers get +4 plus their PIETY Score on Knowledge checks involving religious lore.

Favorite Talent and Profession Trees
Talent Trees: Theologist
Professions: Apothecary, Enchanter, Witchcrafter

No Cost to open talent tree. 5% rate increase on profession tiers. See Talent and Profession Bonuses: Races vs. Classes for how these bonuses work.

Features such as; Companion Pairing, buffs, and various Armaments and Accessories and their Modifiers and Enhancements modify base stats, refer to Basic Rules for more.

Armor Thresholds
Grade: Light (thick Wool, Leather, Padded). Bonus: +1 Protection Score (PROTS) from spiritual attunement; +2 and +2 to PROTS and Theologist Talents if thick Wool is worn.

+1 PROTS and +2 to Theologist Talents if wearing Light or Delicate (Leather or Padded).

Paths and Branches unlock various Armaments not available for Class Tier Abilities.

A Path or Branch's Weapon Requirements include every weapon already available to the Main Class, plus any new weapons that Path or Branch unlocks. A Path or Branch's Armor Threshold also rises without an Armament Penalty, typically half a Grade step above the Tier before it.

Armament Thresholds allow the given Grade and anything lighter. If Armor that is heavier than the Avenger's Threshold is worn, Characters suffer the ensuing Penalties to the Armor's Score (see Armament Penalty, Basic Rules pg. 6).

Example Spell Card - Ward of Cleansing. (Temporary layout, pending final card design.)

Spell Card Main Class: Avenger Path: Cleric Spell: Ward of Cleansing "Holy fire crawls up through cursed flesh or festering rot, called forth with a war-priest's chant, blistering the affliction to ash even as it scours the wound clean. What's left behind steams and stinks of burnt corruption, but it no longer spreads, no longer speaks, no longer belongs to whatever put it there." Action Cost: 1 Action Vitality Cost: 3 Mana Range: 30 ft Requires: Blunt weapon equipped, Medium Grade armor or lighter donned (see readied Armaments pg. 4) Effect: Shoot holy damage, 3d6 + PIETY, to a target currently suffering a curse, disease, or poison effect. That affliction ends immediately if the target takes damage from this Spell. Branch: Null (requires level 21) Module: ASA Crypt v. 0.02 | Ref #Spell002
Cleric Branch Descriptions
▸ Select to Expand i. Holy - the Cleric's default and most balanced expression, a steady shield-and-mace defender. (1h blunt weapon and shield, or 2h blunt weapon, as Cleric default; unlocks Heavy Grade (Sanctified Plate) armor and a Piercing weapon, a blessed spear) (Penalties and Bonuses TBA)
ii. Oracle - a farther-reaching caster who trades armor weight for spell range, wielding only wood or ivory blunt weapons to keep their channeling pure. (2h blunt weapon, wood or ivory only, no metal, or 1h blunt weapon, wood or ivory, and holy symbol in offhand; Light Grade (Ivory-threaded Cloth) armor or lighter) (Penalties and Bonuses TBA)
iii. Warpriest - a dual-wielding Cleric who pairs a blunt main-hand weapon with any offhand blunt weapon, eventually earning a magic slashing weapon in the main hand. (1h (Main) blunt weapon, 1h (Off) any blunt weapon; unlocks Medium Grade (Battle Chain) armor and a 1h (Main) Slashing weapon, must be magic) (Penalties and Bonuses TBA)

Monk Branch Descriptions
▸ Select to Expand i. Chanter - a Monk who channels devotion through music, using a light instrument as a magical focus for their chants. (unarmed strikes plus a light instrument for chants; Light Grade (Songweave Cloth) armor or lighter, and a Magic-channeling chant instrument) (Penalties and Bonuses TBA)
ii. Shapeflow - the most mobile Monk branch, forgoing all but the lightest armor to strike with precise, piercing unarmed blows. (unarmed strikes only; Delicate Grade (Featherwrap Silk) armor only, for maximum mobility; unlocks a 1h Piercing unarmed strike, precise knuckle and joint strikes) (Penalties and Bonuses TBA)
iii. Qirateka - a tankier Monk branch that uses medium armor and bracers to parry blows, drawing enemy attention away from allies with taunts. (unarmed strikes; unlocks Medium Grade (Banded Chain) armor and light bladed hand weapons like tonfa or sai, plus Medium Grade bracers usable for Parry; also gains taunts that draw threat from allies onto themselves) (Penalties and Bonuses TBA)

Barbarian (Playable in Starter Set)

Alignment: All

Fierce and relentless hunters who draw power from primal instinct and raw physical dominance, Barbarians trade refinement for devastation, excelling in brutal melee combat across every environment from frozen mountain peaks to untamed wild plains, where rage is a resource and restraint is a weakness.

‡ Abilities from their respective trees are summarized below. Ability Cards are released with Module and their expansions, supporting various Character Levels, and list the DIFS for any check an Ability requires. Refer pg. 6 for more on Ability Cards.

Note: Main Class baseline stats, Armament requirements and thresholds, and other Class features change depending on the Classes Tier, Path or Branch as noted in each respective Sub-Class.

Favored Races:
Bugbear +5, Hawkbear +5, Ogre† +5, Troll (Bridge) +5, Troll (Mountain) +5, Dwarf (Snow) +5, Neanderthal (Glaciera) +5, Skrath +5, Dwarf (Ash) +5, Elf (Sylvan) +5, Drevane +5, Leshy +5

†Ogre Playable with Starter Set.

Averse Races: Elf (Common) -5, Halfling -5

Refer to Races for details on favored and averse paths and branches.

Passive Abilities:
These passive Abilities belong to the Main Class alone, granted once and active regardless of Tier, Path, or Branch; they are not re-granted, replaced, or duplicated at any Path or Branch.

Blood Frenzy, lasts 6 hours (must be recast every 6 hours to stay active). No mana cost for Main Class Abilities.

Barbzerker, Once Per Day the Barbarian roars when reaches half of their Life they get an extra attack per turn.

When a barbarian reaches 0 Life, they instantly get life equal to their Constitution Trait Score, and get 3 attacks at that turn.

Extra 1d6 + lvl damage on Critical Hits.
Once per encounter, Barbarians can

Flourish a 2h Melee weapon that lowers their target's PROTS at a number equal to their Athletics Score.

Barbarians get +5 feet their base movement speed, once per encounter.

Barbarians get +4 plus their STR Score on Intimidation checks.

Favorite Talent and Profession Trees
Talent Trees: Olympiad
Professions: Field Medic, Hunter, Bounty Hunter, Scout

No Cost to open talent tree. 5% rate increase on profession tiers. See Talent and Profession Bonuses: Races vs. Classes for how these bonuses work.

Features such as; Companion Pairing, buffs, and various Armaments and Accessories and their Modifiers and Enhancements modify base stats, refer to Basic Rules for more.

◆2h Chop or Blunt.

Weapon Types:
◆Martial Melee or Magic Melee for Nature or Spell Abilities respectively; may use TAW or Energy.
◆Restricted to Martial for Melee; wherever a Path or Branch may allow it.

Whenever Blood Frenzy (see Main Class Abilities above) is Active:

◆Weapon Bonus†: Crit add 1d6 + STR (for Melee) AGI (for Shoot).
◆1H Melee: +1 Hit.
◆2H Melee: +2 Hit, +1 Damage.
◆+2 and +2 to Hit and Olympiad Talents if the Skullcrusher Maul (Blunt) or Bloodfang Cleaver (Chop) is wielded.
◆1H Shoot: 0.
◆2H Shoot: 0.

See each path and branch for specifics.

†Reminder: A required weapon must be drawn to perform Abilities from any class's Tier, Path, or Branch; whether referring to the weapon Style, Type, Hand, Range or Grade.

Armor Thresholds
Grade: Light (Fur, Leather). Bonus: +2 to Strength checks; +2 and +2 to †Defense and Olympiad Talents if Fur is worn.

+1 for any other medium Armor and +2 to Olympiad Talents if wearing Light or Delicate.

Paths and Branches unlock various Armaments not available for Class Tier Abilities.

A Path or Branch's Weapon Requirements include every weapon already available to the Main Class, plus any new weapons that Path or Branch unlocks. A Path or Branch's Armor Threshold also rises without an Armament Penalty, typically half a Grade step above the Tier before it.

†This includes Parry if wearing bracers, refer to pg. 2 Traits.

Armament Thresholds allow the given Grade and anything lighter. If Armor that is heavier than the Barbarian's Threshold is worn, Characters suffer the ensuing Penalties to the Armor's Score (see Armament Penalty, Basic Rules pg. 6).

▾ Collapse Armament

Barbarian Main Class Abilities
Each tree below runs Level 1 through 30, Tier (1-3), Path (4-20), Branch (21-30). Each Level offers 3 choices, learn only ONE. See Ability Cards individually for details, see card examples on this page. See Slots and Prerequisites, above, for how a later choice can require an earlier one.
Armaments reminder: Medium Grade armor or lighter; Weapon Style: Slashing or Blunt, 2h, Melee, base loadout (e.g., greataxe, greatsword, warhammer, or maul), see each Path below for how this widens past Level 5. Weapon Type: Martial for Nature Drawn, Magic for Spell Drawn (Spell Drawn is chants, war cries, and spirit-rites, not incantations). Wearing a heavier Grade brings a -5 Armament Penalty per Grade of difference.
Note: See each Classes respective Ability Card for full details; Ability Cards are released with Module and their expansions, supporting various Character Levels, and list the DIFS for any check an Ability requires. Refer pg. 6 for more on Ability Cards.

Bard (Not Playable in Starter Set)

Alignment: All

Musical enchanters who blend performance and combat into a single flowing art, Bards weave spells through melody, rhythm, and song, inspiring allies to supernatural performance, confusing enemies into disarray, and reshaping the battlefield's emotional landscape through instruments that are as much weapon as they are art. Centyrs have a natural affinity for this class.

‡ Abilities from their respective trees are summarized below. Ability Cards are released with Module and their expansions, supporting various Character Levels, and list the DIFS for any check an Ability requires. Refer pg. 6 for more on Ability Cards.

Note: Main Class baseline stats, Armament requirements and thresholds, and other Class features change depending on the Classes Tier, Path or Branch as noted in each respective Sub-Class.

Favored Races:
Centyr +5, Elf (High) +5, Brownling +5, Gnome +5, Halfling† +5

†Halfling Playable with Starter Set.

Averse Races: Ogre -5, Dwarf, Common -5, Orcus -5, Leshy -5, Skrath -5

Refer to Races for details on favored and averse paths and branches.

Passive Abilities:
These passive Abilities belong to the Main Class alone, granted once and active regardless of Tier, Path, or Branch; they are not re-granted, replaced, or duplicated at any Path or Branch.

Bard's Cadence, lasts 6 hours (must be recast every 6 hours to stay active). No mana cost for Main Class Abilities.

Crescendo, Once Per Day the Bard builds to a climactic verse, granting every ally within earshot an extra action on their next turn.

Extra 1d6 + lvl psychic damage on Critical Hits.
Once per encounter, Bards can Flourish their instrument to grant an ally advantage on their next Talent Roll.

Bards get +5 feet their base movement speed, once per encounter.

Bards get +4 plus their CHARISMA Score on Persuasion checks.

Favorite Talent and Profession Trees
Talent Trees: Trader
Professions: Body Artist, Holo-Artist, Cook

No Cost to open talent tree. 5% rate increase on profession tiers. See Talent and Profession Bonuses: Races vs. Classes for how these bonuses work.

Features such as; Companion Pairing, buffs, and various Armaments and Accessories and their Modifiers and Enhancements modify base stats, refer to Basic Rules for more.

Bard Tier Armaments
▸ Select to Expand Armaments Weapon Requirements (Must be readied and drawn to perform Abilities)

Weapon Styles and Hand:
◆1h Instrument (string, drum, or wind).

Weapon Types:
◆Martial for Nature Abilities or Magic for Spell Abilities. TAW and Energy Forbidden.

Whenever Bard's Cadence (see Main Class Abilities above) is Active:

◆Weapon Bonus†: +1 to musical enchantment potency while drawn.
◆1H Melee: 0.
◆2H Melee: 0.
◆Spell: +2 musical enchantment.
◆+2 and +2 to musical enchantment potency and Trader Talents if the Windsong Lute is played.

†Reminder: A required weapon must be drawn to perform Abilities from any class's Tier, Path, or Branch; whether referring to the weapon Style, Type, Hand, Range or Grade.

Armor Thresholds
Grade: Delicate or Light (Cloth, Light Leather). Bonus: +1 Charisma in cloth or light armor; +2 and +2 to Charisma and Trader Talents if Cloth is worn.

+1 Charisma and +2 to Trader Talents if wearing Delicate or Light (Light Leather).

Paths and Branches unlock various Armaments not available for Class Tier Abilities.

A Path or Branch's Weapon Requirements include every weapon already available to the Main Class, plus any new weapons that Path or Branch unlocks. A Path or Branch's Armor Threshold also rises without an Armament Penalty, typically half a Grade step above the Tier before it.

Armament Thresholds allow the given Grade and anything lighter. If Armor that is heavier than the Bard's Threshold is worn, Characters suffer the ensuing Penalties to the Armor's Score (see Armament Penalty, Basic Rules pg. 6).

▾ Collapse Armament

Bard Main Class Abilities
Each tree below runs Level 1 through 30, Tier (1-3), Path (4-20), Branch (21-30). Each Level offers 3 choices, learn only ONE. See Ability Cards individually for details, see card examples on this page. See Slots and Prerequisites, above, for how a later choice can require an earlier one.
Armaments reminder: Delicate or Light armor; Weapon Style: none, 1h Instrument (string, drum, or wind), see each Path below for how this widens past Level 5. Weapon Type: Martial for Nature Drawn, Magic for Spell Drawn (Nature Drawn is struck or beaten directly through the instrument, close and percussive, Spell Drawn is sung or played out at range, not incantations). Wearing a heavier Grade brings a -5 Armament Penalty per Grade of difference.
Note: See each Classes respective Ability Card for full details; Ability Cards are released with Module and their expansions, supporting various Character Levels, and list the DIFS for any check an Ability requires. Refer pg. 6 for more on Ability Cards.
For full versions see each Ability's Card, per module.

Doom Knight (Not Playable in Starter Set)

Alignment Restrictions: Evil

Corrupted warriors who channel death, decay, and necrotic energy into devastating martial combat, Doom Knights serve dark powers with equal parts blade and curse, treating entropy itself as a weapon and the suffering of enemies as fuel for their own continued existence in service of forces mortals were not meant to understand.

‡ Abilities from their respective trees are summarized below. Ability Cards are released with Module and their expansions, supporting various Character Levels, and list the DIFS for any check an Ability requires. Refer pg. 6 for more on Ability Cards.

Note: Main Class baseline stats, Armament requirements and thresholds, and other Class features change depending on the Classes Tier, Path or Branch as noted in each respective Sub-Class.

Favored Races:
Troll (Village) +5, Human† +5, Orcus +5

†Human Playable with Starter Set.

Averse Races: Centyr -5, Elf (Common) -5, Elf (Sylvan) -5, Brownling -5, Halfling -5

Refer to Races for details on favored and averse paths and branches.

Passive Abilities:
These passive Abilities belong to the Main Class alone, granted once and active regardless of Tier, Path, or Branch; they are not re-granted, replaced, or duplicated at any Path or Branch.

Grave Pact, lasts 6 hours (must be recast every 6 hours to stay active). No mana cost for Main Class Abilities.

Deathless March, Once Per Day the Doom Knight refuses to fall, surviving at 1 Life when reduced to 0 and draining Life from the nearest enemy equal to their Resistance Score.

Extra 1d6 + lvl necrotic damage on Critical Hits.
Once per encounter, Doom Knights can Flourish a 2h weapon that lowers their target's Resistance at a number equal to their Toughness Score.

Doom Knights get +5 feet their base movement speed, once per encounter.

Doom Knights get +4 plus their RES Score on Intimidation checks.

Favorite Talent and Profession Trees
Talent Trees: Crypt Raider
Professions: Blacksmith, Engineer, Stonesmith

No Cost to open talent tree. 5% rate increase on profession tiers. See Talent and Profession Bonuses: Races vs. Classes for how these bonuses work.

Features such as; Companion Pairing, buffs, and various Armaments and Accessories and their Modifiers and Enhancements modify base stats, refer to Basic Rules for more.

Doom Knight Tier Armaments
▸ Select to Expand Armaments Weapon Requirements (Must be readied and drawn to perform Abilities)

Weapon Styles and Hand:
◆2h Slashing or 2h Chop.

Weapon Types:
◆Martial for Nature Abilities or Magic for Spell Abilities. TAW and Energy Forbidden.

Whenever Grave Pact (see Main Class Abilities above) is Active:

◆Weapon Bonus†: +1 Damage from necrotic amplification.
◆1H Melee: +1 Hit.
◆2H Melee: +1 Hit, +1 Damage (necrotic amp).
◆+2 and +2 to Hit and Crypt Raider Talents if the Deathless Greatsword (Slashing) or Gravehewn Axe (Chop) is wielded.
◆Spell: +1 necrotic and death magic.

†Reminder: A required weapon must be drawn to perform Abilities from any class's Tier, Path, or Branch; whether referring to the weapon Style, Type, Hand, Range or Grade.

Armor Thresholds
Grade: Heavy or Medium (Plate, Full Chain). Bonus: +2 Armor Score (AS) in plate or heavy chain; +1 PROTS in heavy armor; +2 and +2 to AS and Crypt Raider Talents if Plate is worn.

+1 AS and +2 to Crypt Raider Talents if wearing Heavy or Medium (Full Chain).

Paths and Branches unlock various Armaments not available for Class Tier Abilities.

A Path or Branch's Weapon Requirements include every weapon already available to the Main Class, plus any new weapons that Path or Branch unlocks. A Path or Branch's Armor Threshold also rises without an Armament Penalty, typically half a Grade step above the Tier before it.

Armament Thresholds allow the given Grade and anything lighter. If Armor that is heavier than the Doom Knight's Threshold is worn, Characters suffer the ensuing Penalties to the Armor's Score (see Armament Penalty, Basic Rules pg. 6).

Druid (Not Playable in Starter Set)

Alignment: All

Ancient nature-bound spellcasters who draw power from the living world itself, Druids channel celestial forces, primal animal transformation, and dream-state consciousness to protect and reshape the natural order, equally capable of becoming the predator they summon, calling down starlight as a weapon, or walking through enemy minds while their body sits motionless in the wild.

‡ Abilities from their respective trees are summarized below. Ability Cards are released with Module and their expansions, supporting various Character Levels, and list the DIFS for any check an Ability requires. Refer pg. 6 for more on Ability Cards.

Note: Main Class baseline stats, Armament requirements and thresholds, and other Class features change depending on the Classes Tier, Path or Branch as noted in each respective Sub-Class.

Favored Races:
Firbolg +5, Elf (Common)† +5, Elf (Sylvan) +5, Yawnie +5, Drevane +5, Leshy +5

†Elf (Common) Playable with Starter Set.

Averse Races: Omnè -5

Refer to Races for details on favored and averse paths and branches.

Passive Abilities:
These passive Abilities belong to the Main Class alone, granted once and active regardless of Tier, Path, or Branch; they are not re-granted, replaced, or duplicated at any Path or Branch.

Verdant Attunement, lasts 6 hours (must be recast every 6 hours to stay active). No mana cost for Main Class Abilities.

Wild Shape Ascendant, Once Per Day the Druid fully transforms into a beast form matching their terrain, gaining a Life pool equal to their Constitution Score and the beast's natural attacks for the rest of the encounter.

Extra 1d6 + lvl nature damage on Critical Hits.
Once per encounter, Druids can Flourish their staff to entangle a target, reducing their movement speed by half.

Druids get +5 feet their base movement speed, once per encounter, while in natural terrain.

Druids get +4 plus their KNOWLEDGE Score on nature-related Knowledge checks.

Favorite Talent and Profession Trees
Talent Trees: Scout
Professions: Apothecary, Bioengineer, Carpenter

No Cost to open talent tree. 5% rate increase on profession tiers. See Talent and Profession Bonuses: Races vs. Classes for how these bonuses work.

Features such as; Companion Pairing, buffs, and various Armaments and Accessories and their Modifiers and Enhancements modify base stats, refer to Basic Rules for more.

Armor Thresholds
Grade: Light or Delicate (Hide, Robe). Bonus: +1 to nature-based spell rolls in hide or robes; +2 and +2 to nature Spell rolls and Scout Talents if Hide is worn.

+1 to nature Spell rolls and +2 to Scout Talents if wearing Light or Delicate (Robe).

Paths and Branches unlock various Armaments not available for Class Tier Abilities.

A Path or Branch's Weapon Requirements include every weapon already available to the Main Class, plus any new weapons that Path or Branch unlocks. A Path or Branch's Armor Threshold also rises without an Armament Penalty, typically half a Grade step above the Tier before it.

Armament Thresholds allow the given Grade and anything lighter. If Armor that is heavier than the Druid's Threshold is worn, Characters suffer the ensuing Penalties to the Armor's Score (see Armament Penalty, Basic Rules pg. 6).

Fighter (Not Playable in Starter Set)

Alignment: All

The most adaptable martial class in Essentia, Fighters are defined by mastery of raw combat fundamentals, developing unmatched weapon mastery through sheer repetition and battlefield experience that no trained academic can replicate, making them the most reliable class in sustained combat regardless of the situation they find themselves in.

‡ Abilities from their respective trees are summarized below. Ability Cards are released with Module and their expansions, supporting various Character Levels, and list the DIFS for any check an Ability requires. Refer pg. 6 for more on Ability Cards.

Note: Main Class baseline stats, Armament requirements and thresholds, and other Class features change depending on the Classes Tier, Path or Branch as noted in each respective Sub-Class.

Favored Races:
Troll (Village) +5, Troll (Common) +5, Human† +5, Hobbling +5

†Human Playable with Starter Set.

Averse Races: Elf (Common) -5, Halfling -5

Refer to Races for details on favored and averse paths and branches.

Passive Abilities:
These passive Abilities belong to the Main Class alone, granted once and active regardless of Tier, Path, or Branch; they are not re-granted, replaced, or duplicated at any Path or Branch.

Combat Focus, lasts 6 hours (must be recast every 6 hours to stay active). No mana cost for Main Class Abilities.

Battle-Forged, Once Per Day the Fighter draws on raw battle instinct, gaining a bonus to Hit and Damage equal to their Grit Score for the rest of the encounter.

Extra 1d6 + lvl physical damage on Critical Hits.
Once per encounter, Fighters can Flourish their weapon that lowers their target's Defense at a number equal to their Strength Score.

Fighters get +5 feet their base movement speed, once per encounter.

Fighters get +4 plus their STR Score on Athletics checks.

Favorite Talent and Profession Trees
Talent Trees: Tactician
Professions: Blacksmith, Engineer, Body Artist, Hunter

No Cost to open talent tree. 5% rate increase on profession tiers. See Talent and Profession Bonuses: Races vs. Classes for how these bonuses work.

Features such as; Companion Pairing, buffs, and various Armaments and Accessories and their Modifiers and Enhancements modify base stats, refer to Basic Rules for more.

Fighter Tier Armaments
▸ Select to Expand Armaments Weapon Requirements (Must be readied and drawn to perform Abilities)

Weapon Styles and Hand:
◆Any (Slashing, Blunt, Piercing, or Chop), 1h (Main), 1h (Off), or 2h; unarmed strikes (fist, bare hands, wrapped hands, or leather gloves) also usable and gain a bonus, see Brawler Path for specifics.

Weapon Types:
◆Martial Melee or Magic Melee for Nature or Spell Abilities respectively; may use TAW or Energy.
◆Restricted to Martial for Melee; wherever a Path or Branch may allow it.

Whenever Combat Focus (see Main Class Abilities above) is Active:

◆Weapon Bonus†: Crit add 1d6 + STR (for Melee) AGI (for Shoot).
◆1H Melee: +1 Hit.
◆+2 and +2 to Hit and Tactician Talents if the Ironclad Shortsword is wielded.
◆Shield (Off) +1 PROTS, or a second 1h Weapon (Off) +1 Hit instead (dual-wield).
◆2H Melee: +1 Hit.
◆+2 and +2 to Hit and Tactician Talents if the Warborn Greatblade is wielded.
◆1H Shoot: 0.
◆2H Shoot: 0.

†Reminder: A required weapon must be drawn to perform Abilities from any class's Tier, Path, or Branch; whether referring to the weapon Style, Type, Hand, Range or Grade.

Armor Thresholds
Grade: Versatile (varies by Path). Bonus: +1 Hit when fighting in the armor style matching whichever Path's Armaments are currently donned; +2 and +2 to Hit and Tactician Talents if Half Leather is worn.

+1 Hit and +2 to Tactician Talents whenever wearing Delicate, Light, or Medium Grade otherwise (street clothes, e.g. a leather jacket, jeans, leather gloves, or wraps; Brawler may also wear Medium Grade bracers, see Brawler Path).

Note: Grade and Type still apply to a Fighter's Armaments the same as any other class, this Path's street-clothes framing just emphasizes a class that doesn't lean on traditional Armaments, it isn't an exception to the Grade & Type system itself.

Paths and Branches unlock various Armaments not available for Class Tier Abilities.

A Path or Branch's Weapon Requirements include every weapon already available to the Main Class, plus any new weapons that Path or Branch unlocks. A Path or Branch's Armor Threshold also rises without an Armament Penalty, typically half a Grade step above the Tier before it.

Armament Thresholds allow the given Grade and anything lighter. If Armor that is heavier than the Fighter's Threshold is worn, Characters suffer the ensuing Penalties to the Armor's Score (see Armament Penalty, Basic Rules pg. 6).

Magic User (Not Playable in Starter Set)

Alignment: All

Arcane scholars and innate tricksters who bend reality through illusion, transformation, and raw magical force, Magic Users sacrifice all physical durability for nearly limitless manipulation of both the material and immaterial world, equally comfortable turning an enemy into a toad, stepping sideways through time, or opening a rift to somewhere else entirely.

‡ Abilities from their respective trees are summarized below. Ability Cards are released with Module and their expansions, supporting various Character Levels, and list the DIFS for any check an Ability requires. Refer pg. 6 for more on Ability Cards.

Note: Main Class baseline stats, Armament requirements and thresholds, and other Class features change depending on the Classes Tier, Path or Branch as noted in each respective Sub-Class.

Favored Races:
Imperials +5, Gnome +5, Miceling +5

None Playable with Starter Set.

Averse Races: Ogre -5, Dwarf, Common -5, Neanderthal (Glaciera) -5

Refer to Races for details on favored and averse paths and branches.

Passive Abilities:
These passive Abilities belong to the Main Class alone, granted once and active regardless of Tier, Path, or Branch; they are not re-granted, replaced, or duplicated at any Path or Branch.

Spellweaver's Trance, lasts 6 hours (must be recast every 6 hours to stay active). No mana cost for Main Class Abilities.

Reality Fracture, Once Per Day the Magic User tears a seam in reality, dealing arcane damage equal to twice their Knowledge Score to one target.

Extra 1d6 + lvl arcane damage on Critical Hits.
Once per encounter, Magic Users can Flourish their arcane focus that lowers their target's Defense at a number equal to their Wit Score.

Magic Users get +5 feet their base movement speed, once per encounter.

Magic Users get +4 plus their KNOWLEDGE Score on Knowledge checks involving arcane lore.

Favorite Talent and Profession Trees
Talent Trees: Hacker
Professions: Enchanter, Artificer, Gem Crafter

No Cost to open talent tree. 5% rate increase on profession tiers. See Talent and Profession Bonuses: Races vs. Classes for how these bonuses work.

Features such as; Companion Pairing, buffs, and various Armaments and Accessories and their Modifiers and Enhancements modify base stats, refer to Basic Rules for more.

Magic User Tier Armaments
▸ Select to Expand Armaments Weapon Requirements (Must be readied and drawn to perform Abilities)

Weapon Styles and Hand:
◆1h Arcane Focus (wand, orb, or tome).

Weapon Types:
◆Martial for Nature Abilities or Magic for Spell Abilities. TAW and Energy Forbidden.

Whenever Spellweaver's Trance (see Main Class Abilities above) is Active:

◆Weapon Bonus†: +1 to spell Hit while drawn.
◆1H Melee: 0.
◆2H Melee: 0.
◆Spell: +2 arcane; +1 illusion and transformation.
◆+2 and +2 to spell potency and Hacker Talents if the Runebound Tome is channeled.
◆Spellbook (Off) +1 spell potency, or a free hand (Off) +1 Hit to spell attacks instead (somatic gesture).

†Reminder: A required weapon must be drawn to perform Abilities from any class's Tier, Path, or Branch; whether referring to the weapon Style, Type, Hand, Range or Grade.

Armor Thresholds
Grade: Delicate (Silk Robe). Bonus: +1 spell potency in full arcane robes with no armor; +2 and +2 to spell potency and Hacker Talents if a Silk Robe is worn.

Paths and Branches unlock various Armaments not available for Class Tier Abilities.

A Path or Branch's Weapon Requirements include every weapon already available to the Main Class, plus any new weapons that Path or Branch unlocks. A Path or Branch's Armor Threshold also rises without an Armament Penalty, typically half a Grade step above the Tier before it.

Armament Thresholds allow the given Grade and anything lighter. If Armor that is heavier than the Magic User's Threshold is worn, Characters suffer the ensuing Penalties to the Armor's Score (see Armament Penalty, Basic Rules pg. 6).

Marksman (Playable in Starter Set)

Alignment: All

Precision-focused ranged combatants who dominate at distance through superior positioning, weapon mastery, and tactical patience, striking long before enemies can close the gap through either heavy bow work, black powder weaponry, or the swift shortbow mobility of a Ranger who turns natural terrain into cover, an edge on the hunt, and a marked shot the moment prey steps into the open.

‡ Abilities from their respective trees are summarized below. Ability Cards are released with Module and their expansions, supporting various Character Levels, and list the DIFS for any check an Ability requires. Refer pg. 6 for more on Ability Cards.

Note: Main Class baseline stats, Armament requirements and thresholds, and other Class features change depending on the Classes Tier, Path or Branch as noted in each respective Sub-Class.

Favored Races:
Elf (Common)† +5, Wood Elf +5, Brownling +5, Ratkin +5, Yawnie +5, Omnè +5

†Elf Playable with Starter Set.

Averse Races: None recorded.

Refer to Races for details on favored and averse paths and branches.

Passive Abilities:
These passive Abilities belong to the Main Class alone, granted once and active regardless of Tier, Path, or Branch; they are not re-granted, replaced, or duplicated at any Path or Branch.

Steady Hand, lasts 6 hours (must be recast every 6 hours to stay active). No mana cost for Main Class Abilities.

Deadeye, Once Per Day the Marksman lines up the perfect shot, dealing damage equal to twice their Dexterity Score to one target, ignoring half their Defense.

Extra 1d6 + lvl piercing damage on Critical Hits.
Once per encounter, Marksmen can Flourish their ranged weapon that lowers their target's Defense at a number equal to their Dexterity Score.

Marksmen get +5 feet their base movement speed, once per encounter.

Marksmen get +4 plus their DEXTERITY Score on Perception checks.

Favorite Talent and Profession Trees
Talent Trees: Scout
Professions: Hunter, Tinker, Engineer

No Cost to open talent tree. 5% rate increase on profession tiers. See Talent and Profession Bonuses: Races vs. Classes for how these bonuses work.

Features such as; Companion Pairing, buffs, and various Armaments and Accessories and their Modifiers and Enhancements modify base stats, refer to Basic Rules for more.

Armor Thresholds
Grade: Medium or Light (Chain, Leather). Bonus: +1 Hit with Shoot weapons in leather or lighter; +2 and +2 to Hit and Scout Talents if Leather is worn.

Paths and Branches unlock various Armaments not available for Class Tier Abilities.

A Path or Branch's Weapon Requirements include every weapon already available to the Main Class, plus any new weapons that Path or Branch unlocks. A Path or Branch's Armor Threshold also rises without an Armament Penalty, typically half a Grade step above the Tier before it.

Armament Thresholds allow the given Grade and anything lighter. If Armor that is heavier than the Marksman's Threshold is worn, Characters suffer the ensuing Penalties to the Armor's Score (see Armament Penalty, Basic Rules pg. 6).

Overseer (Not Playable in Starter Set)

Alignment Restrictions: Lawful

Holy martial commanders who lead from the front in divine plate, Overseers combine exceptional armor mastery with auras, command abilities, and divine authority, inspiring allies who stand near them, breaking the will of evil through proximity alone, and serving as the unmovable standard around which armies and adventuring parties alike can rally and hold.

‡ Abilities from their respective trees are summarized below. Ability Cards are released with Module and their expansions, supporting various Character Levels, and list the DIFS for any check an Ability requires. Refer pg. 6 for more on Ability Cards.

Note: Main Class baseline stats, Armament requirements and thresholds, and other Class features change depending on the Classes Tier, Path or Branch as noted in each respective Sub-Class.

Favored Races:
Dwarf (Common)† +5, Human† +5

†Dwarf and Human Playable with Starter Set.

Averse Races: Bast -5, Ogre -5, Troll (Bridge) -5, Troll (Sand) -5, Drāco Blood -5, Drow -5, Dwarf (Glimmerstone) -5, Gnoll -5, Orcus -5, Goblorc -5, Pinkling -5, Ratkin -5, Drevane -5, Emberscale -5, Imperials -5, Leshy -5, Primal -5, Skrath -5

Refer to Races for details on favored and averse paths and branches.

Passive Abilities:
These passive Abilities belong to the Main Class alone, granted once and active regardless of Tier, Path, or Branch; they are not re-granted, replaced, or duplicated at any Path or Branch.

Overseer's Oath, lasts 6 hours (must be recast every 6 hours to stay active). No mana cost for Main Class Abilities.

Unbroken Vanguard, Once Per Day the Overseer plants their banner, granting every ally within earshot a shield equal to their Piety Score that absorbs damage before Life.

Extra 1d6 + lvl holy damage on Critical Hits.
Once per encounter, Overseers can Flourish their weapon to grant an ally a free Defense roll.

Overseers get +5 feet their base movement speed, once per encounter.

Overseers get +4 plus their PIETY Score on Knowledge checks involving religious lore.

Favorite Talent and Profession Trees
Talent Trees: Theologist
Professions: Blacksmith, Stonesmith, Enchanter, Shieldwright

No Cost to open talent tree. 5% rate increase on profession tiers. See Talent and Profession Bonuses: Races vs. Classes for how these bonuses work.

Features such as; Companion Pairing, buffs, and various Armaments and Accessories and their Modifiers and Enhancements modify base stats, refer to Basic Rules for more.

◆Shield (Off) +1 AS, or Holy Symbol (Off) +1 to all Heals or Smites instead.
◆2H Melee: +1 Hit.
◆+2 and +2 to Hit and Theologist Talents if the Radiant Greatsword is wielded.
◆Spell: +1 divine healing and smite.

†Reminder: A required weapon must be drawn to perform Abilities from any class's Tier, Path, or Branch; whether referring to the weapon Style, Type, Hand, Range or Grade.

Armor Thresholds
Grade: Heavy or Medium (Plate, Full Chain). Bonus: +2 Armor Score (AS) in plate or full chain; +1 Protection Score (PROTS) when shield is equipped; +2 and +2 to AS and Theologist Talents if Plate is worn.

+1 AS and +2 to Theologist Talents if wearing Heavy or Medium (Full Chain).

Paths and Branches unlock various Armaments not available for Class Tier Abilities.

A Path or Branch's Weapon Requirements include every weapon already available to the Main Class, plus any new weapons that Path or Branch unlocks. A Path or Branch's Armor Threshold also rises without an Armament Penalty, typically half a Grade step above the Tier before it.

Armament Thresholds allow the given Grade and anything lighter. If Armor that is heavier than the Overseer's Threshold is worn, Characters suffer the ensuing Penalties to the Armor's Score (see Armament Penalty, Basic Rules pg. 6).

Shaman (Not Playable in Starter Set)

Alignment: All

Spirit-world intermediaries who bridge the gap between the living and the ancient, Shamans channel elemental forces, ancestor spirits, and deep earth magic through rituals, mantras, and voodoo-adjacent mysticism, as comfortable calling lightning through a tribal drum as they are raising the bones of the fallen to serve their cause or whispering fire through their own breath.

Refer to Races for details on favored and averse paths and branches.

Passive Abilities:
These passive Abilities belong to the Main Class alone, granted once and active regardless of Tier, Path, or Branch; they are not re-granted, replaced, or duplicated at any Path or Branch.

Totem Rite, lasts 6 hours (must be recast every 6 hours to stay active). No mana cost for Main Class Abilities.

Ancestor's Call, Once Per Day the Shaman summons the spirits of their lineage, healing all allies within earshot for an amount equal to their Willpower Score.

Extra 1d6 + lvl spirit damage on Critical Hits.
Once per encounter, Shamans can Flourish their totem that lowers their target's Resistance at a number equal to their Intuition Score.

Shamans get +5 feet their base movement speed, once per encounter.

Shamans get +4 plus their KNOWLEDGE Score on Knowledge checks involving spirit lore.

Favorite Talent and Profession Trees
Talent Trees: Theologist
Professions: Alchemist, Apothecary, Witchcrafter

No Cost to open talent tree. 5% rate increase on profession tiers. See Talent and Profession Bonuses: Races vs. Classes for how these bonuses work.

Features such as; Companion Pairing, buffs, and various Armaments and Accessories and their Modifiers and Enhancements modify base stats, refer to Basic Rules for more.

Shaman Tier Armaments
▸ Select to Expand Armaments Weapon Requirements (Must be readied and drawn to perform Abilities)

Weapon Styles and Hand:
◆1h or 2h Totem or Staff.

Weapon Types:
◆Martial for Nature Abilities or Magic for Spell Abilities. TAW and Energy Forbidden.

Whenever Totem Rite (see Main Class Abilities above) is Active:

◆Weapon Bonus†: Crit add 1d6 + WILLPOWER.
◆1H Melee: 0 (ritual weapons, clubs).
◆+2 and +2 to spell potency and Theologist Talents if the Bonecarved Totem is wielded.
◆Bone Rattle (Off) +1 spell potency, or Buckler (Off) +1 PROTS instead.
◆2H Melee: +1 Hit (staves, totems).
◆+2 and +2 to spell potency and Theologist Talents if the Stormwood Staff is wielded.
◆Spell: +2 elemental and spirit; +1 ritual and curse.

†Reminder: A required weapon must be drawn to perform Abilities from any class's Tier, Path, or Branch; whether referring to the weapon Style, Type, Hand, Range or Grade.

Armor Thresholds
Grade: Light or Delicate (Hide, Ritual Garments). Bonus: +1 spell potency in ritual garments or hide; +2 and +2 to spell potency and Theologist Talents if Hide is worn.

+1 to spell potency and +2 to Theologist Talents if wearing Light or Delicate (Ritual Garments).

Paths and Branches unlock various Armaments not available for Class Tier Abilities.

A Path or Branch's Weapon Requirements include every weapon already available to the Main Class, plus any new weapons that Path or Branch unlocks. A Path or Branch's Armor Threshold also rises without an Armament Penalty, typically half a Grade step above the Tier before it.

Armament Thresholds allow the given Grade and anything lighter. If Armor that is heavier than the Shaman's Threshold is worn, Characters suffer the ensuing Penalties to the Armor's Score (see Armament Penalty, Basic Rules pg. 6).

Sorcerer (Playable in Starter Set)

Alignment: All

Born rather than trained, Sorcerers carry raw arcane power in their blood and channel it through staff and cloth into spells of extraordinary breadth, their magic growing more unstable and powerful the deeper they push their natural gift, making them capable of the most dramatic single effects in Essentia at the price of anything resembling physical resilience.

‡ Abilities from their respective trees are summarized below. Ability Cards are released with Module and their expansions, supporting various Character Levels, and list the DIFS for any check an Ability requires. Refer pg. 6 for more on Ability Cards.

Note: Main Class baseline stats, Armament requirements and thresholds, and other Class features change depending on the Classes Tier, Path or Branch as noted in each respective Sub-Class.

Favored Races:
Drāco Blood +5, Dwarf (Red) +5, Elf (High) +5, Helf +5

None Playable with Starter Set.

Averse Races: None recorded.

Refer to Races for details on favored and averse paths and branches.

Passive Abilities:
These passive Abilities belong to the Main Class alone, granted once and active regardless of Tier, Path, or Branch; they are not re-granted, replaced, or duplicated at any Path or Branch.

Arcane Ascendance, lasts 6 hours (must be recast every 6 hours to stay active). No mana cost for Main Class Abilities.

Bloodborn Surge, Once Per Day the Sorcerer unleashes raw innate magic, dealing arcane damage equal to twice their Focus Score to one target, with the Sorcerer taking damage equal to half that amount.

Extra 1d6 + lvl arcane damage on Critical Hits.
Once per encounter, Sorcerers can Flourish their staff that lowers their target's Defense at a number equal to their Focus Score.

Sorcerers get +5 feet their base movement speed, once per encounter.

Sorcerers get +4 plus their FOCUS Score on Knowledge checks involving arcane lore.

Favorite Talent and Profession Trees
Talent Trees: Traveler
Professions: Enchanter, Gem Crafter, Body Artist

No Cost to open talent tree. 5% rate increase on profession tiers. See Talent and Profession Bonuses: Races vs. Classes for how these bonuses work.

Features such as; Companion Pairing, buffs, and various Armaments and Accessories and their Modifiers and Enhancements modify base stats, refer to Basic Rules for more.
